findings.title: Classify explicit HTTP 413 before parsing its untrusted body
findings.detail: The 413 branch follows resp.json(). A synthetic HTTP 413 body with 30000 nested arrays raises RecursionError outside the local ValueError/TypeError handler. Primary and format-recovery requests both then escape as generic ProviderResponseError, bypassing the processor typed-413 persistence branch and allowing another classification after SQS replay.
findings.fix: Move the exact 413 fixed safe exception before any body decode; primary and recovery must reject body access entirely for status 413.

findings.title: Show the distinct guest caller before offering a permanent-ban action
findings.detail: For synthetic guest actor42/caller700123, the generic neutral reply names neither caller nor guest while displaying Ban. Executing that real callback path permanently targets700123. The existing guest review explicitly identifies both identities and warns that invocation does not prove intent; the new branch removes those safeguards from the administrator decision.
findings.fix: Use neutral guest-specific translated text containing separately resolved BOT and TARGET, explain that the Ban action permanently affects the identified personal caller and invocation alone proves no intent. Preserve no-caller no-button/server-side refusal.
